title: Software Development Engineer Intern
description:
HackerRank helps companies like NVIDIA, Amazon, and Microsoft hire and upskill the next generation of developers based on skills, not pedigree. Our platform is trusted by over 2,500 of the world’s most innovative companies to build strong engineering teams ready for what’s next.
Software has entered an era where humans and AI build side by side. As this shift accelerates, the definition of strong technical talent is changing. We give companies better ways to identify and invest in next-generation skills.
People at HackerRank care deeply about the impact of their work and sweat the small details so our customers can be wildly successful with products they genuinely love to use. We move with urgency and believe great outcomes come from high standards.

This is a 6-month full-time onsite internship (Jan - June 2027).

Please apply only if you're available full-time to work from the Bengaluru office for the entire duration.

If you're obsessed with writing great code that will be used by other great engineers around the world, read on - this just may be the perfect role for you. HackerRank is looking for high-potential Hacker Interns to join our team of world-class full-time Hackers as we build the most engaged community of Developers.

Life as an intern at HackerRank

World-class mentors, great culture, amazing people and opportunities to make a difference all in a real-world scenario and right at the beginning of your career! If this sounds exciting, read on...

Each one of you will be paired with a mentor, who will support you throughout your internship.

You get to push your code to prod and contribute to meaningful & real-world projects right from your first month.

Transparent communication is one of the principles that  guides us. You’ll have access to all the information needed including the company’s progress every week directly from the Executive team.

You’ll have direct access to all employees in the company and can always challenge the status quo, enabling you to be more data driven.

Whether you're graduating and seeking a full-time position after your internship, or hoping to return for another internship next year, you'll be considered for a returning offer during your internship.

title: Software Engineer, Internship
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organisations around the world use data. As a Software Engineer Intern, you’ll have an opportunity to grow more quickly than you ever envisioned, as you contribute high-quality code directly to Palantir Gotham, Palantir Foundry, or Palantir Apollo: products that are deployed at some of the most important institutions across the public and private sectors. You'll create features used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world. Palantir's Product Development organisation is made up of small teams of Software Engineers, each focusing on a specific aspect of a product. For example, you might join a team that builds a Foundry front-end application, or a component of the Gotham release infrastructure. We encourage communication and collaboration among teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different aspects of each product.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As a Software Engineer, you are involved throughout the product lifecycle - from idea generation, design, and prototyping to execution and shipping while also being paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth and success. You'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our customers' problems and build products that tackle them. One of the most effective ways to understand what our users need is to meet them. You may receive an opportunity to tour the assembly line at an auto-manufacturer or join a counter-terror analyst at their desk to really understand their mission and difficulties.
 
SWE principles include: 
 
• Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end in spite of obstacles we may encounter.
• Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers and Product Reliability Engineers. We also partner with our business development teams (Forward Deployed Engineers, Deployment Strategists) in order to understand and solve our customers' problems.
• Trust: We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities, and don't micromanage. We want people to have the space to think for themselves, while feeling supported by their team.
 
 
Technologies We Use
 
It doesn’t matter what languages you know when you join us, but it does matter that you can write clean, effective code and learn new languages quickly. Our software is constantly evolving, so we need engineers who can do the same. Alongside peers that bring diverse experience - whether you’re a former university TA,

title: Software Engineer, Internship - Query Engines
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
We are a software engineering team applying open-source data technologies to some of the world's hardest and most important problems. We build the data processing infrastructure that underpins Palantir Foundry, supporting applications that help hospitals care for more patients, help clinical teams coordinate timely diagnoses, and keep essential supplies moving through global disruption.
 
You will work deep inside the systems that make this possible: how computations are represented, how query plans are optimised, how operators execute, and how data is read and written efficiently. We build on and extend Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, and Apache Iceberg, bringing advances in open-source engines and table formats into the demanding environments our customers operate in. Our work serves many products and workloads across Foundry, including no-code pipelines, interactive analysis, and the processing that keeps the Ontology up to date.
 
Working alongside experienced engineers, you will take on real problems in our production systems. That could mean writing a new planning rule, adding a capability to a native execution engine, or making large tables faster to scan. You will see your work through design, code review, testing, and release. Correctness, compatibility, and predictable performance are central to everything we build, and you will learn how to deliver all three.
 
Join us if you want to learn how modern data systems work from the inside and apply that knowledge to consequential problems.

Technologies We Use

Java, Scala, Rust, and Python

Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, Apache Comet, and Velox for data processing and query execution

Apache Iceberg for table management and catalog interoperability

Apache Arrow and Apache Parquet for in-memory data processing and columnar storage

Gradle and Cargo for builds, and GitHub for collaboration

You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here.

What We Value

Curiosity about how data systems work, from query optimisers and execution operators to file formats and distributed processing

A high bar for correctness and a willingness to dig until you understand why something behaves the way it does

Comfort following a problem across languages, services, and layers of the stack

A practical approach to performance, grounded in measurement rather than intuition

Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback

Interest in applying deep systems engineering to real-world problems, with empathy for the people who depend on our software

What We Require

Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Sci

title: 2027 - Summer Software Engineer Intern, Dublin
description:
We’re seeking curious minds like yours to collaborate with full-time engineers and cross functional teammates, learn development standard methodologies, and gain practical software engineering experience.
Software engineering interns are fully integrated into software engineering teams across our Product and Technology organization. Interns spend their summer pushing production-level code to make lasting contributions across MongoDB’s products and services for our internal teams, external customers, and developer end users.
This is a 10 week internship starting in June 2027.

What we are looking for in you (qualifications)

In the process of receiving a Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

Have a foundation in computer science theory, with proficiencies in data structures, algorithms, and software design.

Fluent in any one of the following programming languages: Java, Python, Go, C++, Javascript, Node.js - or a comparable object-oriented programming language.

Have a minimum of one quarter/semester remaining in university studies after the internship concludes. Graduation date in, Spring 2028, Summer 2028, Fall 2028, Spring 2029 or Summer 2029.

Must be authorized to work in Ireland and provide the Company with copies of all relevant documents, if requested. Company sponsorship may be available for eligible candidates applying for certain roles.

What you'll find at MongoDB

Authentic Culture: A workplace where you are encouraged to bring your whole self to work, we believe that Embracing the Power of Differences is the best way to broaden our own perspectives and foster innovation.

Personalized Mentorship: Pair up with an engineering Mentor, a Program Advisor from the Early Talent Recruitment Team, and an
Employee Resource Group
(ERG) Guide to foster your growth.

Career Coaching Sessions: Access to a tailored training program designed uniquely for interns’ personal and professional development.

Work-Life Harmony: Embrace "Bloom for Interns" with access to mental and physical health benefits, paid time off, free lunch, and more!

Impactful Projects: Contribute to projects where you can Make it Matter - your meaningful work will see the light of day.

Exclusive Networking: Attend "Speaker Series" and "Get to Knows" to connect with our executives and departmental leaders.

Vibrant Community: Build connections with fellow interns and join after-work social events, virtual gatherings, and local city activities to create connections and friendships.

Relocation Support: Housing to allow you to comfortably settle into your new location.

Path to Full-Time: A chance to see if MongoDB is where you see yourself long term with the possibility of receiving a full time offer at the end of the summer!

MongoDB internships are full-time (40 hours/week) for 10 consecutive weeks lasting from dates in June until August. All interns are considered hybrid employees, designated the "in office" working mode

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Warp Speed
Warp Speed builds on years of excellence in manufacturing to resurrect & revitalize the American Industrial Base. FDSEs on Warp Speed work directly with customers from the factory floor to the board room to understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions using data.
 
As Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organizations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the most important industries and institutions globally!
 
The Original Forward Deployed Software Engineer 
At Palantir, the Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) role isn’t just a job title: it’s the blueprint. We pioneered this unique position, embedding talented engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDSE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.
 
FDSEs work side by side with our customers, rapidly understanding their toughest issues; architecting and building solutions that leverage business-critical data and the latest advancements in AI to solve them. Whether it’s “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks to optimize power grids?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global food supply chain to deliver life-saving aid on time?”, you’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.
 
You’ll have the rare opportunity to gain deep insight into and directly influence some of the world’s most critical industries and institutions. By building on Palantir’s powerful platforms leveraging integrated cutting-edge AI, you’ll help organizations unlock the full potential of their data to make smarter, faster decisions.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As an FDSE, you’ll experience the autonomy of a startup, with the resources, mentorship, and stability of an established tech company. • Collaborating with fellow engineers on architecture and design decisions

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Internship
description:
Le poste

Les Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSE) travaillent directement avec les clients afin de comprendre rapidement leurs problèmes les plus importants et ainsi concevoir et implémenter des solutions qui vont utiliser leurs données afin de résoudre ces problématiques. Nos clients s’appuient sur les plateformes de Palantir pour certaines de leurs opérations les plus critiques, et les projets débutent souvent par une question ouverte, par exemple : « Comment évaluer le risque d’incendie de forêt et, par conséquent, comment optimiser le réseau électrique ? » ou « Comment évaluer rapidement notre chaîne d’approvisionnement alimentaire et l’adapter afin d’apporter à temps une aide vitale ? » En tant que FDSE, vous appliquez votre capacité à résoudre les problèmes, votre créativité et vos compétences techniques pour aider les organisations à exploiter au mieux leurs données et avoir ainsi un impact réel sur le monde. Vous avez l’opportunité d’obtenir des informations rares et de contribuer à certaines des industries et institutions les plus importantes au monde.

Responsabilités principales

En tant que stagiaire chez FDSE, vos responsabilités s’apparentent à celles que l’on trouve dans une petite start-up, tout en bénéficiant des ressources, de la stabilité et de l’accompagnement d’une entreprise technologique bien établie. Vous travaillerez en petites équipes avec une supervision minimale et serez responsable de l’exécution de bout en bout de projets à enjeux élevés. Votre journée peut consister à discuter de l’architecture avec d’autres ingénieurs, à gérer des données à grande échelle, à coder une application web personnalisée, à discuter avec l’équipe dirigeante du client ou à établir une stratégie pour votre équipe.

Les stagiaires FDSE sont traités exactement comme des ingénieurs à temps plein, et bénéficient d’une grande liberté et d’une grande autonomie dans leur travail. Ils assument la responsabilité des projets et des résultats réels sur lesquels nos clients comptent.

Nos principes:
Impact : nous gérons des projets significatifs et enthousiasmants qui rendent le monde meilleur.
Responsabilité : nous menons nos projets du début à la fin, en surmontant tous les obstacles que nous pourrions rencontrer. Nous nous faisons mutuellement confiance afin de gérer efficacement le temps et les priorités et donner aux individus l’espace nécessaire pour réfléchir par eux-mêmes.
Collaboration : nous travaillons en interne avec des personnes d’horizons variés, tels que d’autres FDSE, des équipes Produits et des Deployment Strategists. Nous travaillons également en externe avec nos clients, souvent sur site, afin de comprendre et de répondre à leurs problèmes.
Développement : nous pensons que l’apprentissage par l’expérience est l’une des meilleures écoles et nous nous encourageons nous-mêmes tout comme nos pairs à rechercher de nouveaux défis et de nouvelles opportunités de croissance, ainsi qu’à trouver de nouvelles façons d’innover et de part

description:

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Forward Deployed Engineering is a radical commitment to the outcome. This is Palantir’s operating ethos. We pioneered this unique position, embedding engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.

From hospital beds to factory floors, Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed themselves in the customer’s reality until the problem is theirs. This requires walking many miles in a customer’s shoes, building past the perimeter of what the product currently offers, and deviating from every pre-existing formula to solve the problem. Whether that problem is “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks across a power grid?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global supply chain to deliver critical parts on time?”, you’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
To solve mission-critical problems by deploying software and AI into the high stakes operations of the world’s leading institutions. This requires a ruthless commitment to truth-seeking and prioritizing real outcomes. 

The work is difficult. The stakes are real. You will work in small, high-trust teams and own projects end-to-end, from the first conversation with a customer, to shipping the product that changes how they operate. You will embed with the customer, the chaos, and the consequences, and will be entrusted with real ownership to: 
Collaborate with engineers to make architecture and design decisions
Wrestle with data at a scale that breaks assumptions and demands invention
Build custom applications, LLM workflows, and production solutions engineered for a specific customer's reality
Own relationships with stakeholders from the users in the weeds to the executives making the calls
 As an Intern, you will be entrusted with responsibility on day 1 and expected to learn quickly. You will not be handed a low-risk or unimportant project. You will not be shielded from the customer, the chaos, or the consequences. FDEs are entrusted with real ownership, operating with real autonomy, and held to a real standard, no matter their tenure.

The drive to solve your customer’s problem. This can translate to:

Going where you’re needed most
— Embed where and when it matters. Expect 25–50% travel, depending on team and location.

Agency
— You learn continuously, make decisions with incomplete information, and don't wait to be told what to do next.

Embracing the ambiguity
— You operate effectively in teams that mix technical

description:
This Sr Data Analyst will join our analytics org within the Executive Insights team, which is responsible for synthesizing revenue and operational data from across the company to measure the trajectory and overall health of the business.

You will work closely with partner teams in Analytics, FP&A, Accounting, Cloud Billing, and Sales Operations to not only drive alignment on business performance narratives, but also to drive company wide transparency and data democratization for company key metrics.

Data pipelines, visualizations, root cause analyses, and deep dives generated by this team routinely empower MongoDB’s executive team to make data-informed decisions. This is a high visibility role that offers exposure to senior leadership via the team’s support of the office of the CFO.

We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Gurugram for our hybrid working model.

Responsibilities

Deep dive on performance metrics from across the company to surface drivers of business growth to enable data-driven decision making at the executive level

Produce insights to answer requests ahead of critical reporting periods, including earnings and investor days

Partner with the rest of the team to own the end-to-end delivery of recurring consumption and revenue reports (weekly, monthly, and quarterly) ensuring they're accurate, timely, and trusted by stakeholders

Proactively identify and fix data quality issues, broken pipelines, or reporting discrepancies

Document metric definitions, report logic, and data lineage

Skills & Attributes

The ideal candidate excels equally in data wrangling, pipelining, and storytelling, and shares a passion for automation and continuous process improvement

4+ years in an analyst, data, or BI role with meaningful ownership of key business metrics reporting

Strong SQL skills; comfortable writing and optimizing queries against large-scale warehouses (Trino, BigQuery, or similar)

Working proficiency in Python for data transformation, automation, or analysis

Hands-on Tableau or similar BI tool experience

Experience with agent-driven development practices

Experience working with consumption-based or usage-based revenue data (subscription, metered billing, or usage analytics a strong plus)

Nice-to-have: exposure to analytics engineering practices (dbt, data modeling, testing frameworks)

And most importantly, passionate about using data to help guide strategic decision making

title: Staff Data Analyst

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems.
Co-create the future with us
as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.
An overview of this role
As a Staff Data Analyst, you'll turn raw data into actionable insights that inform strategic decisions across GitLab's global Support Engineering organization. You'll design dashboards, reports, and data models that help leaders monitor performance, optimize costs, and improve customer outcomes. You'll also promote data innovation by experimenting thoughtfully and working through complex problems.
What you'll do

Own annual operating plan and capacity planning through data modeling and validation that support workforce and budget decisions.

Build and maintain utilization and team-performance scorecards, including automated alerting that surfaces trends in real time.

Analyze Support Economics, including cost-per-ticket modeling, self-service savings, and product quality costs.

Develop performance indexes and heatmaps that identify product areas and customers using the most support resources.

Lead dashboarding for AI adoption and return on investment, measuring the business impact of AI-driven initiatives across Support Engineering.

Partner with go-to-market teams on predictive analytics and churn-prevention models that identify at-risk customers.

Define and refine unified customer-schema requirements to create consistent data across systems and a single source of truth.

title: Information Security Engineer - Infrastructure Security
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
We're looking for an Information Security Engineer who can think broadly about how infrastructure is built, attacked, defended, and improved. You may have deep experience in one area—such as endpoint security, Active Directory, Data Loss Prevention, cloud security, identity, or detection and response—but you’re motivated by solving security problems across the environment.

As an Information Security Engineer focused on infrastructure security, you'll help protect Palantir's global endpoints, servers, identity systems, applications, networks, and data flows. You'll work across teams to reduce attack surface, improve defensive controls, investigate security events, and turn security findings into durable architectural and operational improvements.

This is not just a corporate security role; the adversaries we face are sophisticated. We need someone who understands both the details and the broader system: how a weakness in one part of the environment can create risk somewhere else, how controls interact, and how to build security improvements that hold up in practice.

Core Responsibilities

Design, implement, and improve security controls across endpoints, servers, identity systems, cloud services, SaaS applications, networks, and data flows.

Drive security posture improvements through hardening standards, configuration management, vulnerability remediation, access controls, monitoring, and ongoing validation.

Assess security risks in new platforms, products, architectures, vendors, and services, and turn findings into practical recommendations and engineering work.

Build and maintain automation for security operations, including configuration validation, drift monitoring, patching, access reviews, policy enforcement, alert triage, and security hygiene.

Partner with Identity, Infrastructure, Engineering, Legal, and other Information Security teams to strengthen security architecture and address recurring risks.

Turn insights from assessments, red team exercises, incident investigations, and operational reviews into durable fixes, such as configuration changes, architectural improvements, policy updates, and automation.

Build expertise in one or more security domains while contributing across the broader infrastructure security lifecycle.

What We're Looking For

Experience securing one or more major infrastructure domains, such as Windows, macOS, Linux, Active Directory, cloud platforms, SaaS applications, networking, identity systems, or enterprise endpoints.

A broad infrastructure security mindset and curiosity about systems beyond your primary area of expertise.

Familiarity with common infrastructure attack paths, adversary tact

About the Team

The Agentic Security Engineering team is a horizontal, shared services engineering team that enables every Databricks security function AI-native. We enable building the AI agents, "personas," and own the shared platform that security teams across the org (Detection & Response, Threat Intelligence, Vulnerability & Product Security, Red Team, GRC, and Continuous Monitoring) build on to operate at machine speed, safely and reliably.

Senior Staff Security Software Engineer

You will operate across organizational boundaries, aligning engineering and security leaders on platform architecture, driving adoption of common patterns, and resolving complex technical problems that affect multiple security functions. Shared Security AI Platform Architecture

Set engineering standards for reliability, observability, evaluation, incident response, cost instrumentation, and safe production deployment.

Make high-leverage build, buy, and adopt decisions that keep the platform focused on security-specific capabilities while using Databricks platform primitives wherever they meet the need.

Design the platform to support secure multi-agent workflows, tool registries, policy-aware orchestration, and agent-to-agent collaboration.

Reliable and Safe Agentic Systems at Scale

Lead the design and development of production-grade platform capabilities that enable security personas to operate reliably across a growing AI and security surface.

Define how the platform measures successful runs, latency, failure rates, rollback readiness, safety, governance coverage, trust, autonomy, and business value.

Establish qualification and maturity mechanisms that determine what a security persona may do, what controls it require

title: Security Systems Engineer
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
As a Security Systems Engineer at Palantir, you are responsible for implementing, designing, and maintaining the physical security systems that ensure the protection of Palantir’s people, assets, intellectual property, and reputation. You lead research and evaluations for the latest technology, security infrastructure, policies, procedures, systems, and applications, looking for easy-to-use capabilities that reduce button clicks and ultimately give time back to the operator. You will be collaborating with technical teams to develop and maintain end-to-end project plans and ensure on-time delivery.

Your technical expertise is second only to your integrity and genuine passion for security and technology. As a member of the Global Security and Investigations team, you work with security professionals, architects, lawyers, and software and network engineers to deliver a safe and secure environment for your fellow employees. Palantir is a global company, so you'll lead physical security projects all over the world. You'll work hard to break down barriers between teams by communicating your knowledge and goals effectively across time zones and other physical and virtual barriers. 

*Please note this role is NOT for cyber security or information security positions*

Core Responsibilities

Design and oversee the technical aspects of your projects from conception to full deployment.

Systems naturally break and need maintenance. You'll work with vendors and end users to find the best solutions for a problem, in the shortest possible time.

Leverage both system and software engineering skills in order to address the needs of all teams within Global Safety and Security.

Prepare and document standard operating procedures, protocols, and security standards.

Responsible for scheduling, testing, and implementing enhancements or new releases of server operating systems.

Develop detailed project plans, timelines, budgets, and resource allocation for all project phases.

Regularly present project updates, status reports, and risk summaries to leadership.

Ensure that all deliverables meet internal security policies, regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, NIST, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS), and industry standards.

Validate that implemented security controls are effective and meet project goals before project closure.

Prioritize tasks across competing deadlines and manage scope changes gracefully.

What We Value

Experience supporting Global Security Operations Centers, offices, and remote outposts.

Strong engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics.

Active TS security clearance or willingnes

title: Staff Software Engineer, iOS Platform
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:

The iOS Platform team’s mission is to provide best-in-class experience for iOS development at Airbnb to empower engineers to deliver innovative solutions with high velocity and quality at scale.

We’re ambitious in our vision, and our work spans a large surface area, from frameworks and tooling to build systems, CI, Testing, and AI automations. We maintain and evolve the core libraries & frameworks that underlie most of the Airbnb iOS app and enable product engineers to build great features. Our application is nearly 100% written in Swift and we adopt the latest Apple technologies including SwiftUI, Swift Macros, Swift Testing, and structured concurrency.

The Difference You Will Make:

In this role, you’ll be responsible for driving projects that improve AI agents’ effectiveness across the software development workflow by providing the right tools to get work done efficiently and reliably, with high-quality results.

A Typical Day:

Collaborate with team members & cross functional partners to identify opportunities for improving our developers’ productivity.

Drive roadmap projects and deliver high-quality results to further our mission.

Improve our existing frameworks & toolings to deliver on our ambitious vision.

Your Expertise:

9+ years of industry experience in software development.

Experience building reliable developer tooling in Go.

Experience working with Ruby and maintaining or improving existing tooling.

Experience leveraging Agentic AI to improve software development workflows and drive large scale migrations.

Experience identifying and addressing inefficiencies in AI agent workflows to improve execution time, token efficiency, reliability, and quality.

Experience working in medium- to large-scale codebases.

iOS development experience in Swift, including building applications, libraries, and frameworks.

[Nice to have] Experience designing and developing build systems (e.g. Bazel).

Ability to travel to the San Francisco office for about a week each quarter for gatherings.

Your Location:

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity.

title: Staff Software Engineer - Distributed Data Systems
description:
P-186

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high value challenges that are central to their own missions.

Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark™, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, California to a global organization with over 1000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest growing SaaS companies in the world.

Our engineering teams build highly technical products that fulfill real, important needs in the world. We constantly push the boundaries of data and AI technology, while simultaneously operating with the resilience, security and scale that is critical to making customers successful on our platform.

We develop and operate one of the largest scale software platforms. The fleet consists of millions of virtual machines, generating terabytes of logs and processing exabytes of data per day. At our scale, we regularly observe cloud hardware, network, and operating system faults, and our software must gracefully shield our customers from any of the above.

Modern data analysis employs sophisticated methods such as machine learning that go well beyond the roll-up and drill-down capabilities of traditional SQL query engines. As a software engineer on the Runtime team at Databricks, you will be building the next generation distributed data storage and processing systems that can outperform specialized SQL query engines in relational query performance, yet provide the expressiveness and programming abstractions to support diverse workloads ranging from ETL to data science.

Below are some example projects:

Apache Spark™
: Develop the de facto open source standard framework for big data.

Data Plane Storage
: Deliver reliable and high performance services and client libraries for storing and accessing humongous amount of data on cloud storage backends, e.g., AWS S3, Azure Blob Store.

Delta Lake
: A storage management system that combines the scale and cost-efficiency of data lakes, the performance and reliability of a data warehouse, and the low latency of streaming. Its higher level abstractions and guarantees, including ACID transactions and time travel, drastically simplify the complexity of real-world data engineering architecture.

Delta Pipelines
: It's difficult to manage even a single data engineering pipeline. The goal of the Delta Pipelines project is to make it simple and possible to orchestrate and operate tens of thousands of data pipelines. It provides a higher level abstraction for expressing data pipelines and enables customers to deploy, test & upgrade pipelines and eliminate operational burdens for managing and building high quality data pipelin

title: Staff Software Engineer - Distributed Data Systems

P-186

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high value challenges that are central to their own missions.

Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark™, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, California to a global organization with over 1000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest growing SaaS companies in the world.

Our engineering teams build highly technical products that fulfill real, important needs in the world. We constantly push the boundaries of data and AI technology, while simultaneously operating with the resilience, security and scale that is critical to making customers successful on our platform.

We develop and operate one of the largest scale software platforms. The fleet consists of millions of virtual machines, generating terabytes of logs and processing exabytes of data per day. At our scale, we regularly observe cloud hardware, network, and operating system faults, and our software must gracefully shield our customers from any of the above.

Modern data analysis employs sophisticated methods such as machine learning that go well beyond the roll-up and drill-down capabilities of traditional SQL query engines. As a software engineer on the Runtime team at Databricks, you will be building the next generation distributed data storage and processing systems that can outperform specialized SQL query engines in relational query performance, yet provide the expressiveness and programming abstractions to support diverse workloads ranging from ETL to data science.

Below are some example projects:

Apache Spark™
: Develop the de facto open source standard framework for big data.

Data Plane Storage
: Deliver reliable and high performance services and client libraries for storing and accessing humongous amount of data on cloud storage backends, e.g., AWS S3, Azure Blob Store.

Delta Lake
: A storage management system that combines the scale and cost-efficiency of data lakes, the performance and reliability of a data warehouse, and the low latency of streaming. Its higher level abstractions and guarantees, including ACID transactions and time travel, drastically simplify the complexity of real-world data engineering architecture.

Delta Pipelines
: It's difficult to manage even a single data engineering pipeline. The goal of the Delta Pipelines project is to make it simple and possible to orchestrate and operate tens of thousands of data pipelines. It provides a higher level abstraction for expressing data pipelines and enables customers to deploy, test & upgrade pipelines and eliminate operational burdens for managing and building high quality data pipelin

title: Staff Software Engineer - Distributed Data Systems
description:
P-988

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.

Modern data analysis employs sophisticated methods such as machine learning that go well beyond the roll-up and drill-down capabilities of traditional SQL query engines. As a software engineer on the Runtime team at Databricks, you will be building the next generation distributed data storage and processing systems that can outperform specialized SQL query engines in relational query performance, yet provide the expressiveness and programming abstractions to support diverse workloads ranging from ETL to data science.

Below are some example projects:

Apache Spark™
: Develop the de facto open source standard framework for big data.

Data Plane Storage
: Provide reliable and high performance services and client libraries for storing and accessing humongous amount of data on cloud storage backends, e.g., AWS S3, Azure Blob Store.

Delta Lake
: A storage management system that combines the scale and cost-efficiency of data lakes, the performance and reliability of a data warehouse, and the low latency of streaming. BS (or higher) in Computer Science, related technical field or equivalent practical experience.

Strong foundation in algorithms and data structures and their real-world use cases.

Experience with distributed systems, databases, and big data systems (Apache Spark, Hadoop).

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Data die het verschil maakt
Data is pas waardevol als een organisatie erop kan bouwen. Als Senior Data Engineer bij LINKIT zorg jij daarvoor: je ontwerpt platformen die schaalbaar, betrouwbaar en toekomstbestendig zijn, en je kijkt verder dan de losse pipeline. Klinkt dat als jouw volgende stap?
De uitdaging
Als Senior Data Engineer kom je in dienst bij LINKIT en ga je aan het werk bij toonaangevende opdrachtgevers in mobiliteit, energie en financiële dienstverlening. Je draagt bij aan platformen die er echt toe doen: data-oplossingen voor internationale treinreizen bij NS, moderne beleggingsplatformen bij Robeco en schaalbare data ecosystemen bij EDSN en Stedin. Je ontwerpt en bouwt schaalbare data pipelines in Cloud omgevingen, ontwikkelt betrouwbare datamodellen die organisatiebreed worden gebruikt en denkt actief mee over architectuur, performance en onderhoudbaarheid. Je werkt nauw samen met analytics- en data science-teams om data ML-ready te maken en verbetert bestaande oplossingen waar dat waarde toevoegt. Als Senior Data Engineer maak je zo het verschil op zowel technisch als strategisch niveau.
Je plek binnen LINKIT
Je werkt in de Data Engineering squad: een groep Explorers (zo noemen wij onze collega’s) die elkaar scherp houdt op vakmanschap en samen bouwt aan oplossingen voor complexe dataomgevingen. Kennis delen is de norm, niet de uitzondering. Om de twee weken kom je op vrijdag terug naar het hoofdkantoor in De Meern voor de clubdag, waarin we tijd investeren in leren, verbinden en vooruitkijken.
Lees
hier
meer over de Data Engineering squad.

Wat we vragen
5+ jaar ervaring in data engineering binnen complexe omgevingen.
Sterke programmeervaardigheden in talen zoals Python, Scala en SQL.
Kennis van of ervaring met distributed data processing frameworks/datalakes/orchestrators zoals Spark, Flink, Delta Lake, Iceberg, Airflow, dbt, etc.
Ruime ervaring met production ELT/ETL-pipelines.
Ervaring met batch/streaming dataverwerking.
Ervaring met CI/CD op cloudplatformen.
Ervaring met een cloudplatform zoals Azure, AWS of GCP.
Je communiceert goed in het Nederlands en spreekt vloeiend Engels.
Pré: ervaring met Databricks, Snowflake, MS Fabric of BigQuery.
Voldoe je niet aan elk punt, maar wel nieuwsgierig? Dan komen we alsnog graag met je in contact.
Wat je krijgt
Salaris tussen €5.700-€7.400 per maand (o.b.v. 40 uur, afhankelijk van kennis & ervaring) + 8% vakantiegeld.
Jaarlijkse winstdeling en pensioenregeling.
Hybride werken: op ons hoofdkantoor in De Meern, bij de klant of vanuit huis.
25 vakantiedagen en de mogelijkheid om tijdelijk vanuit het buitenland te werken.
Elektrische leaseauto of mobiliteitsvergoeding.
Netto thuiswerkvergoeding, een goed ingerichte thuiswerkplek en een laptop en telefoon, die je ook privé kunt gebruiken.
Om de twee weken op vrijdag komen alle collega's terug naar ons hoofdkantoor in De Meern, dan investeren wij tot 10% van jouw werktijd in kennisdeling, leren en verbinden (dit noemen wij de clubdag).

title: Staff Software Engineer - Data Platform
description:
P-375

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to tackle technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.

As a Staff Software Engineer working on the Data Platform team, you will leverage bleeding-edge AI developer tools and techniques to help build the Data Intelligence Platform for Databricks that will allow us to automate decision-making across the entire company. You will achieve this in collaboration with Databricks Product Teams, Data Science, and many more. You will define the future of a variety of tools spanning logging, orchestration, data transformation, metric store, governance platforms, and data consumption layers, just to name a few.

The impact you will have:

Design and run the cross-company Data Intelligence Platform, which contains every business and product metric used to run Databricks. You’ll play a key role in developing the right balance of data protection and ease of shareability for the Data Intelligence Platform as we transition to a public company.

Develop tooling and infrastructure to efficiently manage and run Databricks on Databricks at scale, across multiple clouds, geographies, and deployment types. This includes CI/CD processes, test frameworks for pipelines and data quality, and infrastructure-as-code tooling.

Partner with our engineering teams to provide leadership in developing the long-term vision and requirements for the Databricks product.

Build reliable data pipelines and solve data problems using Databricks, our partner’s products, and other OSS tools. Provide early feedback on the design and operations of these products.

Represent Databricks at academic and industrial conferences & events.

What we look for:

BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science or related majors, or equivalent experience.

10+ years of industry experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems.

4+ years of experience providing technical leadership on planet-scale production data systems

Experience leading architecture efforts for performance-sensitive systems (e.g., latency-critical services, multi-tenant platforms, large-scale indexing pipelines).

Strong communication skills and the ability to operate effectively in fast-paced, cross-functional environments.

A strategic mindset with the ability to align engineering execution with longer-term product and company goals.

Passion for mentoring and developing other engineers.

title: Software Engineer, New Grad
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations around the world use data. In this role, you’ll have an opportunity to grow more quickly than you ever envisioned as you contribute high-quality code directly to Palantir Gotham, Palantir Apollo, or Palantir Foundry: products that are deployed at some of the most important institutions across the public and private sectors. You'll create features used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters in countries around the world. Palantir's Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers, each focusing on a specific aspect of a product. For example, you might join a team that builds a Foundry front-end application, or a component of the Gotham release infrastructure. We encourage communication and collaboration among teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll also have the opportunity to learn about other business areas.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As a Software Engineer, you are involved throughout the product lifecycle - from idea generation, design, and prototyping, to execution and shipping, all while also being paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth and success. You'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our customers' problems and build products that tackle them. One of the most effective ways to understand what our users need is to meet them. You may receive an opportunity to tour the assembly line at an auto-manufacturer or join a counter-terror analyst at their desk to really understand their mission and difficulties.
 
SWE principles include:
 
•  Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end in spite of obstacles we may encounter.
•  Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers and Product Reliability Engineers. We also partner with our business development teams (Forward Deployed Engineers, Deployment Strategists) in order to understand and solve our customers' problems.
•  Trust: We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities, and don't micromanage. We want people to have the space to think for themselves, while feeling supported by their team.
 
Technologies We Use
 
It doesn’t matter what languages you know when you join us; what matters is that you can write clean, effective code and learn new languages quickly. Our software is constantly evolving, so we need engineers who can do the same. Alongside peers that bring diverse experience - whether you’re a former university Teaching

The Role
We are a software engineering team applying open-source data technologies to some of the world's hardest and most important problems. We build the data processing infrastructure that underpins Palantir Foundry, supporting applications that help hospitals care for more patients, help clinical teams coordinate timely diagnoses, and keep essential supplies moving through global disruption.
 
You will work deep inside the systems that make this possible: how computations are represented, how query plans are optimised, how operators execute, and how data is read and written efficiently. We build on and extend Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, and Apache Iceberg, bringing advances in open-source engines and table formats into the demanding environments our customers operate in. Our work serves many products and workloads across Foundry, including no-code pipelines, interactive analysis, and the processing that keeps the Ontology up to date.
 
Working alongside experienced engineers, you will take on real problems in our production systems. That could mean writing a new planning rule, adding a capability to a native execution engine, or making large tables faster to scan. You will see your work through design, code review, testing, and release. Correctness, compatibility, and predictable performance are central to everything we build, and you will learn how to deliver all three.
 
Join us if you want to learn how modern data systems work from the inside and apply that knowledge to consequential problems.

Technologies We Use

Java, Scala, Rust, and Python

Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, Apache Comet, and Velox for data processing and query execution

Apache Iceberg for table management and catalog interoperability

Apache Arrow and Apache Parquet for in-memory data processing and columnar storage

Gradle and Cargo for builds, and GitHub for collaboration

You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here.

What We Value

Curiosity about how data systems work, from query optimisers and execution operators to file formats and distributed processing

A high bar for correctness and a willingness to dig until you understand why something behaves the way it does

Comfort following a problem across languages, services, and layers of the stack

A practical approach to performance, grounded in measurement rather than intuition

Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback

Interest in applying deep systems engineering to real-world problems, with empathy for the people who depend on our software

What We Require

Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Sci

-
help ons de tandartspraktijken naar een hoger niveau tillen!

Ben jij een ervaren ontwikkelaar met een passie voor innovatie en softwareontwikkeling? Dan zoeken wij jou! Wat ga je doen?
Applicaties bouwen en optimaliseren:
Jij ontwikkelt en verbetert onze C#- en Blazor-applicaties om ze nog beter te maken.
Innovatieve functionaliteiten ontwerpen:
Samen met je team creëer je nieuwe modules en features die het verschil maken.
Problemen oplossen:
Jij lost bugs en technische uitdagingen op met oplossingen die werken.
Samenwerken en kennis delen:
Je deelt ideeën, best practices en inzichten met je team en andere ontwikkelaars.
Processen verbeteren:
Jij denkt mee over verbeteringen in onze software en ontwikkelprocessen.
Herken jij jezelf hierin?
Wij zoeken iemand die analytisch en resultaatgericht is, met een sterke focus op efficiënte oplossingen. Je bent communicatief vaardig en kunt zowel technische als niet-technische concepten helder uitleggen. Je hebt uitgebreide ervaring met C# en .NET, en ervaring met Blazor of Microsoft Azure is een pré. Je werkt gestructureerd en hebt oog voor detail.

Wat vragen we van jou?
HBO/WO werk- en denkniveau;
Minimaal 7 jaar werkervaring in softwareontwikkeling;
Ervaring in Agile-omgevingen is een pluspunt;
Vloeiend Nederlands en Engels, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk;
Ruime expertise met C# en .NET; Blazor is een pré;
Ervaring met Microsoft Azure is een pré;
Kennis van het zorgdomein is een pré.

Wat hebben wij voor jou in petto?
Een uitdagende rol:
In een dynamisch en groeiend bedrijf waar je veelzijdigheid en variatie vindt.
Fijne werksfeer:
Een informele omgeving waar je volop de ruimte krijgt om jezelf te ontwikkelen.
Teamspirit:
Werk met een gezellig en enthousiast team en blijf fit met wekelijkse sportactiviteiten onder begeleiding van een personal trainer!
Flexibiliteit:
Geniet van flexibele werktijden, kies voor een werkweek vanaf 32 uur en ruil feestdagen in voor dagen die jou beter uitkomen.
Goede arbeidsvoorwaarden:
Een laptop, pensioenregeling, teamuitjes, kwartaalborrels, en een vrijdagmiddagborrel met je collega's.
Ruimte voor persoonlijke groei
: Wij bieden volop kansen voor professionele ontwikkeling, van trainingen en opleidingen tot begeleiding, zodat jij je talenten kunt benutten

Eerst maak je telefonisch kennis met onze Recruiter. En daarna maak je kennis met de leidinggevende en/of een directe collega. Is er een klik? Dan volgt er een verdiepend gesprek. Daarnaast nodigen we je uit om een dagdeel mee

title: Research Engineer, AI Monitoring
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role

Our team builds, tests, deploys, and monitors the classifiers that block internal agents from taking dangerous actions. These classifiers run across RL, evals, and internal deployments, and are designed to catch things like sandbox escape attempts or exfiltration of sensitive data.

When a classifier flags an action, it can
block the action before the tool call runs, end the task, and alert a human
. This is one layer of a defence-in-depth with several layers that reinforce each other: what our classifiers flag feeds into offline monitoring, and the findings from that go back into better classifiers and safer environment design.

The work combines research and production engineering:

The research problem is building high recall and high precision classifiers to catch rare, novel, and sometimes adversarial behaviour. There are also several narrow research questions to answer - for example, how to deploy safety classifiers inside training environments without incentivising models to evade them. Some research also builds on the multi-stage designs described in our work on
Claude Code auto mode
and
Constitutional Classifiers
.

The engineering problem is shipping these classifiers into the critical path of research and product work. These classifiers need to cover a huge volume of traffic while operating within cost, latency and availability constraints.

Day to day, much of our work is done with Claude: you'll direct agents to run experiments and ship code, and review what they produce. That moves the hard part of the job towards deciding what to do and in what order. Additionally, organisation, communication, and prioritisation skills matter a great deal as our classifiers sit in the path of many other teams' work.

Key responsibilities

Design, train, and evaluate classifiers that detect unsafe agent actions in real time, owning pieces such as prompted models, trained classifiers, or probes on model internals

Deploy, tune and operate these classifiers in the critical path of internal agents, RL training, and evaluations, and own their accuracy, reliability, latency, cost, and failure behaviour

Build the datasets, labelling pipelines, and evaluations that allow us to measure and improve our classifiers and harm taxonomies

Partner with red teaming colleagues to stress-test our classifiers, and harden them against what they find

Work with the teams whose agents, environments, and evaluations we run on, so that false positives get fixed quickly without weakening protection

Contribute to the team's direction, including what to build, what to partner on, and where to invest
